seoTitle: How to Get Your Freshdesk API Key (and Why It Might Be Missing)
metaDescription: Find your Freshdesk API key under Profile Settings, get past the View API key captcha, test it with basic auth, and understand why Free-plan and unverified accounts don't show a key at all.
intro:
Freshdesk's API key lives on your personal profile page, not in Admin settings, which is where most people look first. Each agent has their own key, and anything that uses it acts with that agent's permissions.

This guide covers where the key sits, the captcha newer accounts show before revealing it, how to test it with a single request, and what to do if it leaks. It also covers the two reasons the key doesn't appear at all: a Free plan, or an agent account that hasn't been verified yet.
prerequisites: A Freshdesk account on a paid plan. Freshdesk's help centre states API access starts on paid plans and the key isn't shown on the Free plan
A verified agent account (the key is only displayed once the agent is verified)

steps.heading: Open Profile Settings
steps.body: Click your profile picture in the top-right corner of Freshdesk and choose Profile Settings. The page is titled My Profile Settings and holds settings tied to you as an individual agent: time zone, language, email signature, and preferences such as Focus Mode and Undo send. Account-wide Admin settings are a separate area and don't contain the key.

image.caption: The My Profile Settings page, showing time zone, language, and signature fields alongside personal preferences like Focus Mode and Undo send.

steps.heading: Reveal and copy the key
steps.body:
The key sits in the right-hand pane, in a card labelled Your API Key next to Profile Details (name, email, phone). On the account in the recording the key is displayed directly. Freshdesk's current help article describes a View API key option instead, which asks you to complete a captcha before showing the string. If you see that button, click it and finish the captcha.

Copy the key straight into the tool, script or password manager that needs it. Don't park it in a plain text file or a chat thread. The key authenticates as you, with your role's permissions, so anyone holding it can read and change Freshdesk data as you.

image.caption: The top of the profile page with Your API Key displayed next to Profile Details, and a Reset API Key button underneath it.

steps.heading: Test it with one read request
steps.body:
Freshdesk's API uses HTTP basic authentication with the API key as the username and any placeholder as the password. The developer docs use X. A quick test from a terminal looks like this: curl -u YOUR_API_KEY:X https://yourdomain.freshdesk.com/api/v2/tickets

Requests must go over HTTPS, and every endpoint lives under https://yourdomain.freshdesk.com/api/v2/. If you're building the Authorization header by hand, Base64-encode the whole apikey:X string first. A missing encoding step is the usual reason a correct key gets rejected. Run a read like this before wiring up anything that writes data.

steps.heading: Reset the key if it's exposed
steps.body:
If the key ends up in a public repository, a screenshot or anywhere it shouldn't be, click Reset API Key under the key on the same page. Resetting revokes the old key, and Freshdesk notes it disconnects every app that was using it. Each of those integrations stops working until you paste in the new key, so make a list of where the key is used before you reset.

For integrations a whole team depends on, consider a dedicated agent account for the connection. That way one person leaving or resetting their key doesn't break it.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no API key on the Profile Settings page
troubleshooting.cause: The account is on the Free plan, where Freshdesk doesn't provide API access, or the agent hasn't been verified yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the plan under Admin billing and confirm the agent has completed verification. Freshdesk also suggests trying another browser or clearing cache and cookies if the key still doesn't appear.

troubleshooting.problem: Requests return 401 even though the key was copied correctly
troubleshooting.cause: The key and password placeholder weren't Base64-encoded in the Authorization header, or the request went to HTTP instead of HTTPS.
troubleshooting.fix: Send apikey:X Base64-encoded, or let your HTTP client handle basic auth (curl -u does this). Make sure the URL starts with https:// and uses your own Freshdesk subdomain.

troubleshooting.problem: Several integrations broke at the same time
troubleshooting.cause: Someone clicked Reset API Key, which disconnects every app using the old key.
troubleshooting.fix: Copy the new key from Profile Settings and update each integration.

faq.question: Where is the Freshdesk API key?
faq.answer: Profile picture (top right) > Profile Settings, in the right-hand pane. It's on your personal profile, not in Admin settings. Newer accounts show a View API key button with a captcha before the key appears.

faq.question: Does every agent get their own key?
faq.answer: Yes. Each agent has a separate key, and API calls made with it follow that agent's role permissions. Freshdesk's help centre notes that installing marketplace apps and setting up integrations needs an administrator's key.

faq.question: Can I use the API on Freshdesk's Free plan?
faq.answer: No. Freshdesk states API access is available from paid plans onwards, and the key isn't visible on Free accounts.

faq.question: What goes in the password field?
faq.answer: Anything. Freshdesk's API docs use X. The API key goes in the username field of basic authentication.
